question: What share of myristic acid (C14:0) was measured in the macaw palm almond oil evaluated as a heat-transfer fluid, and what did Goncalves and Amaral report?
rendered:
According to the document "Thermophysical and Chemical Evaluation of Macaw Palm Almond Oil as a Biobased Heat-Transfer Fluid Candidate for Medium-Temperature Solar Thermal Applications", page 4, Table 1 reports the fatty-acid composition of macaw almond oil. 

The share of myristic acid (C14:0) in the macaw palm almond oil evaluated as a heat-transfer fluid was 9.41%.

Gonçalves reported 9.3% and Amaral reported 9.41%.
